qs.q: A 32-year-old man notices multiple small, 1 to 2 mm white papules arranged in a neat row around the corona of his glans penis. He is asymptomatic and concerned they might be genital warts. What is the correct management strategy?
o: Reassurance because these are normal papules
Screening for syphilis with specific tests
Biopsy and excision with margin removal
qs.e: Pearly penile papules are a normal anatomical variant found around the corona of the glans in about 15% of post-pubertal men and are not caused by HPV. They require no treatment unless requested for cosmetic reasons.
qs.s: Penile Conditions: Benign Lesions, Premalignant Disease and Penile: MCQs

qs.q: A 50-year-old woman develops invasive cervical carcinoma. Which virus is most strongly associated with this malignancy? HPV 16 and 18 are the high-risk oncogenic types. HPV 6 and 11 cause genital warts but are low-risk for malignancy. ---
o: HPV type 6, a low‑risk genital wart virus
HPV type 11, a low‑risk genital wart virus
HPV type 16, a high‑risk oncogenic virus
HPV type 40, a rare cutaneous papillomavirus
HPV type 42, a low‑risk cutaneous papillomavirus
qs.e: High‑risk HPV 16 is most strongly linked to invasive cervical cancer.
